```python
# Check which users are scoped and which own orders
scope_check = await run_command("""cd /workspace && python -c "
import sqlite3, json
conn = sqlite3.connect('world.db')
conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row

# Get scoped user IDs (same logic as CLI)
rows = conn.execute(\"SELECT user_id, skill_ids_json FROM users WHERE skill_ids_json LIKE '%state-customer-support%'\").fetchall()
scoped = [r['user_id'] for r in rows]
print(f'Scoped user_ids: {scoped}')

# Get distinct customer_ids from state-customer-support orders
order_custs = conn.execute(\"SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM orders WHERE source_skill='state-customer-support'\").fetchall()
order_cust_ids = [r['customer_id'] for r in order_custs]
print(f'Order customer_ids: {order_cust_ids}')

# Check overlap
in_both = set(scoped) & set(order_cust_ids)
only_orders = set(order_cust_ids) - set(scoped)
print(f'In both: {in_both}')
print(f'Only in orders (not scoped): {only_orders}')

# Check if the order-owning users exist in users table with the right skill
for uid in only_orders:
    r = conn.execute('SELECT user_id, skill_ids_json FROM users WHERE user_id=?', (uid,)).fetchone()
    if r:
        print(f'  {uid} skill_ids: {r[\"skill_ids_json\"]}')
    else:
        print(f'  {uid} NOT in users table')
conn.close()
"
""")
print(scope_check)
```
